summary: Re-verification packet. Proved mechanically that no Java file changed since the a62849c5 test pass: the `diff --git a/sequencer/...` section of rc-final.txt and rc-M4.3b-r3.txt hash identically (8df20082...), and the three staged blobs match. check-tdd green with 29 reds, every one bound to sha256 b01784667339... which is exactly the staged and worktree LeaseManagerTest.java, so the reds bind the committed bytes rather than an older file. check-test-integrity green. Suite 483 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, matching the row's claim. The three new backlog rows are accurate against the code I can read: renew() does let the IOException escape with held/heldVersion untouched (M4.3d's looser 'nearly a full TTL' bound is the one that actually holds, and it does not contradict M4.3b's 'up to a full TTL', which is a non-attained upper bound); tryAcquire's unexpired early return at LeaseManager.java:140-142 does leave `held` untouched, and M4.3e is right that the clear must be conditional on holderPodId/epoch since an instance may legitimately hold the lease it just read; there are exactly four synchronized sites as M4.3c states. No ID collisions (M4.3b/c/d/e one row each) and every referenced ID resolves (M4.8, M4.10, M4.12, M0.53, M4.1, M4.7, ADR-0007). On the question put to me directly: I withdraw my earlier justification. It was false, and for the reason review gave -- determinism does not come from controlling the scheduler, it comes from parking a thread at a chosen point INSIDE the critical section using a store call as the blocking primitive, which converts an unobservable race into a determined order. Two accuracy defects in M4.3c's row remain, recorded as minors below.

findings.title: M4.3c names StoreFakes.GatedCommit as the mechanism, but sequencer cannot reach it and it gates the wrong method
findings.failure_scenario: GatedCommit lives in ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/StoreFakes.java -- a plain test source set, not testFixtures -- and ingest depends on sequencer, so the dependency cannot be reversed and a sequencer test cannot import it. There is no testFixtures gate fake in binstore-spi either (its testFixtures holds only the three conformance suites, none of which mention CountDownLatch). Second, GatedCommit gates putIfAbsent ONLY; putIfMatch is a straight pass-through to the delegate, so it cannot park a thread inside the TAKEOVER read-decide-CAS cycle at all. And its single shared `release` latch releases every blocked caller at once, which on the putIfAbsent path parks BOTH contenders and then frees them together -- that reproduces the race rather than determining it, so the assertion would be flaky rather than falsifying. An implementer taking the row literally writes the import, fails to compile, and then has to re-derive the design the row claimed to have handed them. The row should say: a call-selective gated decorator in sequencer's OWN test sources (StatBlindStore in this very commit is the precedent that sequencer writes its own decorators), gating a chosen invocation of putIfMatch, with a second latch so the test can order A's CAS after B's completion.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Not applicable to the staged tests -- this is an accuracy defect in a todo row, and it does not weaken anything in this commit.

findings.title: M4.3c promises 'all four sites' but at least one of the four is an equivalent mutant under any deterministic T1 test
findings.failure_scenario: The row opens by measuring that removing synchronized from all four sites leaves the suite green, which reads as a promise that the task closes when all four are pinned. The interleave the row describes -- gate A inside its CAS, let B run the full cycle, release A, assert held() is present (under the mutation the losing thread's adopt(Optional.empty()) clears held/heldVersion on the same instance and wipes out the winner's belief) -- kills the mutation on tryAcquire, and a variant kills it on renew. It cannot kill it on held(), whose body is a single reference read: removing synchronized there changes only memory visibility, and a visibility bug is not deterministically observable at T1. Left as written, M4.3c gets closed by one test while three sites stay unpinned and the row asserts coverage it does not have -- exactly the pattern this backlog already hit twice (M4.3 round 2's `"ttl"` substring equivalent mutants, and M4.3b round 2's endpoint pinned on the cold-start path only). The row should name which sites it can pin and say plainly that held() is not among them. One further shaping constraint the row omits, because it is the thing that bites first: with synchronized PRESENT the second thread blocks on the monitor BEFORE it reaches any store call, so the test must not use 'thread B completed' as its synchronisation point -- awaiting that deadlocks the correct build, and testing.md leaves no Thread.sleep escape hatch.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Removing `synchronized` from `held()` (LeaseManager.java:112) survives the gated-store interleave M4.3c describes, and survives any deterministic T1 test, because the mutant differs from the original only in JMM visibility.
